findings.description: The EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so its contents may be stored unencrypted unless an account-level default happens to apply. This leaves attached data and derived snapshots without an explicit encryption guarantee.

The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. User data is readable through instance metadata and AWS describe APIs to authorized principals, and credentials in IaC/source must be treated as compromised.

No metadata_options configuration requires IMDSv2 tokens. The instance can therefore use IMDSv1, allowing an SSRF flaw on the web server to potentially retrieve instance metadata and any attached role credentials.

The security group permits TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration to the entire internet. SSH access should be restricted to approved management source ranges or a controlled access path.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This enables unrestricted command-and-control and data exfiltration from a compromised instance.
The flow-log archive bucket has no explicit server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network-flow records are therefore not guaranteed to be encrypted at rest by this Terraform configuration.
